description: Implement the full routing policy engine in the `routing` crate (tasks P4.1-P4.5, architecture.md Section 6): the RoutingPolicy async trait + request/decision types, the three signal families (complexity/privacy/cost), the automatic default policy, the manual-override precedence resolver, and the policy registry. Because routing will now path-depend on `providers`/`domain` (which carry crates.io deps transitively), MOVE `routing` from `[workspace] members` to `[workspace] exclude` in hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml and add per-crate fmt/build/clippy/test steps for it to the routine `build` CI job. This feature also updates the orchestrator-core smoke test call site that references `routing::placeholder()`. Independent of FEAT-002's pipeline wiring except that FEAT-002 depends on the API this feature defines.
steps: Create the working branch: from /projects/agent-harbor run `git checkout -b phase-4-routing-pipeline` off main (commit bccd1bc). All work lands on this branch.

routing/Cargo.toml: add path deps on `providers` (path = "../providers") and `domain` (path = "../domain") plus the crates.io deps the engine needs, pinned as CONCRETE version literals (NOT {workspace=true}, since routing becomes an excluded crate with no workspace root): `async-trait = "0.1"` (RoutingPolicy async trait), `serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }` + `serde_json = "1"` (CostBudget/decision serde + rationale JSON if needed), `thiserror = "2"` (RoutingError). Add `[dev-dependencies] tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt"] }` for #[tokio::test]. Mirror the self-contained-manifest comment style used in crates/orchestrator-core/Cargo.toml. Reconcile: routing REUSES domain::{ManualRoute, PrivacyTag, RouteSource} and providers::{AvailableModel, Capabilities, ChatMessage, TokenPrice, AgentPersona via domain} rather than duplicating them.

routing/src/policy.rs (P4.1): define the `RoutingPolicy` async trait `{ fn id(&self)->&str; async fn decide(&self, req:&RoutingRequest)->Result<RoutingDecision,RoutingError>; }` (use #[async_trait::async_trait]). Define RoutingRequest { messages: Vec<providers::ChatMessage>, privacy_tags: Vec<domain::PrivacyTag>, persona: Option<domain::AgentPersona>, manual_override: Option<domain::ManualRoute>, conversation_pref: Option<domain::ManualRoute>, available: Vec<providers::AvailableModel>, budget: Option<CostBudget> }. Define RoutingDecision { provider_id: String, model: String, rationale: String, source: domain::RouteSource } and a helper to convert it into a domain::RouteMetadata (or document that pipeline builds RouteMetadata from it). Define CostBudget (e.g. { max_cost_per_message: Option<f64>, remaining_budget: Option<f64> } - a token/price budget signal per Section 6.1) deriving Debug/Clone/Serialize/Deserialize with rename_all=camelCase. Define RoutingError (thiserror) with variants including at least NoCandidate/PrivacyConstraintUnsatisfiable/CapabilityUnsatisfiable/ManualRouteRejected/ManualRouteUnavailable, each carrying a display-safe message. Re-export domain::{ManualRoute, PrivacyTag, RouteSource} and providers::AvailableModel from policy.rs (or crate root) so P4.1's named types are all reachable from `routing`. Derive Debug on all structs so tests can {:?} them; do NOT derive/Debug-format any trait object.

routing/src/signals.rs (P4.2): implement the three signal families from Section 6.2. (a) Complexity: a `TaskComplexity` scale (e.g. enum Low/Medium/High or a 0.0..=1.0 score) estimated by heuristics over RoutingRequest.messages - total message text length, message count, presence of code/structured cues (fenced code blocks, JSON/braces, 'function'/'class'/'algorithm'/'refactor' keywords), and whether tools or vision are required. Low complexity biases toward a capable LOCAL model; high complexity biases toward a stronger cloud model. (b) Privacy: a function that reads Vec<PrivacyTag> and returns whether local routing is a HARD constraint (LocalOnly or Confidential force local; Custom does not by itself). (c) Cost: a per-candidate cost estimate from providers::TokenPrice (input+output per Mtok) using an estimated token count from the request, honoring an optional CostBudget; LOCAL models are zero cost (their AvailableModel.price is TokenPrice::ZERO). Define a `RequiredCapabilities` derivation (tools_required if the request carries any tools / persona demands tools; extend for vision if present) used as a hard filter. Document the pricing SOURCE explicitly (comes from providers::AvailableModel.price, which the tauri command derives from the persisted AppConfig pricing table; local = zero). Unit-test each signal.

routing/src/policies/auto_default.rs (P4.3): implement `AutoDefaultPolicy` implementing RoutingPolicy (id = "autoDefault"). decide(): (1) FILTER candidates FIRST by hard constraints - drop any AvailableModel that cannot satisfy required capabilities (e.g. tools_required && !capabilities.tools), and if a privacy hard-constraint applies, keep ONLY local candidates (identify local via provider kind/id heuristic: the pipeline/available list must let routing tell local from cloud - use a convention such as AvailableModel whose price == TokenPrice::ZERO OR a provider_id/kind marker; PREFER a robust signal - see note). (2) If the hard-constraint filter leaves NO candidate under a LocalOnly/Confidential tag, FAIL CLOSED: return Err(RoutingError::PrivacyConstraintUnsatisfiable) - never fall back to a cloud model. (3) RANK the surviving candidates by a weighted blend of quality-for-complexity (higher complexity prefers higher-capability/known-stronger models; use max_context and a capability score as proxies) and cost (cheaper/local preferred when quality needs are met; honor persona routing_hint PreferLocal/PreferQuality/PreferCheap/PreferSpeed and CostBudget as biases). (4) Populate a human-readable `rationale` naming which signals drove the choice (e.g. 'high task complexity + no privacy constraint favored cloud model X; within budget'). source = RouteSource::Automatic. NOTE on local detection: add a small, well-documented helper (e.g. a field or convention) so 'local' is unambiguous rather than guessing from price; if AvailableModel lacks a local marker, derive locality by matching provider_id against a passed-in set OR document that LmStudio/GenericOpenAI-with-loopback are local - choose the cleanest approach that does NOT require changing the `providers` public API, and document the decision in the module doc. Tests: complexity scoring chooses local vs cloud; LocalOnly forces local and FAILS CLOSED when no local candidate; cost bias prefers cheaper when quality is adequate; capability filtering excludes tool-incapable models when tools are required.

routing/src/policies/manual_override.rs (P4.4): implement `ManualOverrideResolver` that WRAPS an active automatic RoutingPolicy (hold Arc<dyn RoutingPolicy>). Its decide() applies Section 6.3 precedence: (1) if req.manual_override is Some -> use it with source=Manual; (2) else if req.conversation_pref is Some -> use it with source=ConversationPin; (3) else delegate to the wrapped automatic policy (source=Automatic). For (1) and (2), the manual route STILL passes hard-constraint validation: if a LocalOnly/Confidential tag applies and the chosen provider/model is NOT local (or is not present as a local candidate in req.available), REJECT with Err(RoutingError::ManualRouteRejected) carrying an explanatory message ('manual route <provider>/<model> would send local-only data to the cloud'). Also validate the manual route resolves to a known AvailableModel with satisfying capabilities where tools are required (reject with an explanatory error if not). Build the RoutingDecision rationale to explain the manual choice ('per-message override', 'per-conversation pin'). Tests: per-message override beats pin beats automatic; a manual choice violating a privacy tag is rejected with an explanatory error; a valid manual local route under LocalOnly is accepted.

routing/src/policies/registry.rs (P4.5): implement `PolicyRegistry { policies: HashMap<String, Arc<dyn RoutingPolicy>>, active: String }` per Section 6.4. Methods: new()/with defaults (register AutoDefaultPolicy as the built-in automatic policy and set it active), register(policy), set_active(id)->Result (error if unknown), active_id(), and a `resolve(req)` entry point that wraps the currently-active automatic policy in the ManualOverrideResolver precedence and returns the RoutingDecision. The `active` id is the persisted selection (AppConfig.active_routing_policy) - document that the tauri layer/pipeline reads/writes it; the registry itself just holds the selectable active id. Test: default active is autoDefault; set_active to unknown errors; resolve routes a manual override even though autoDefault is active (proves the manual resolver wraps the active policy).

routing/src/lib.rs: replace the placeholder module wiring. Keep `pub mod policy; pub mod signals; pub mod policies { pub mod auto_default; pub mod manual_override; pub mod registry; }`. REMOVE `pub fn placeholder()` and its smoke test. Add ergonomic crate-root re-exports (ALPHABETICALLY ORDERED, matching the convention in other crates): RoutingPolicy, RoutingRequest, RoutingDecision, RoutingError, CostBudget, AutoDefaultPolicy, ManualOverrideResolver, PolicyRegistry, and the reused domain/providers types the public API surfaces. Write a crate-level //! doc explaining the crate now carries transitive crates.io deps (via providers/domain) and is therefore under [workspace] exclude, built in CI - AUDIT this doc comment for clippy::doc_overindented_list_items (list continuation lines ~3 spaces after //!).

orchestrator-core/src/lib.rs: update the smoke test that calls `routing::placeholder()` - replace it with a reference to a real routing item now that placeholder is gone (e.g. construct `routing::PolicyRegistry::default()`/new and assert its active_id, mirroring how the smoke test references providers::builtin_registry and mcp_client::namespace_tool). Keep the test meaningful.

hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml: MOVE `crates/routing` from the `members` array to the `exclude` array. Update the surrounding comments: the `members` list may now legitimately contain no offline-buildable-with-deps crate - explain that routing gained transitive crates.io deps (through its path deps on providers/domain) so it joined the excluded set, following the SAME pattern as the other excluded crates; add routing to the excluded-crate rationale list and to the EXIT PATH note (add routing to the networked `cargo build -p ...` list). Keep the [workspace.dependencies] table intact. If members becomes empty, keep the array present (empty) with a comment explaining why - do NOT delete the members key. Verify `cargo build --workspace` behavior is still coherent (it will simply build nothing/less offline; that is acceptable and documented).

.github/workflows/ci.yml: add routing to the routine `build` job. Add a `cargo fmt (check, routing)` step alongside the other per-crate fmt-check steps near the top. Add `cargo build (routing)`, `cargo clippy (routing) --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test (routing)` steps via `--manifest-path crates/routing/Cargo.toml`, placed in DEPENDENCY ORDER (after providers and domain, before/near orchestrator-core since orchestrator-core path-depends on routing). Add an explanatory comment block mirroring the other excluded-crate sections (why routing moved to exclude: transitive crates.io deps via providers/domain; tests use no live network). Update the top-of-file IMPORTANT WORKSPACE ARRANGEMENT comment and the 'only crate that remains an offline-buildable members entry' sentence to reflect routing's move. Do NOT touch the matrix (ubuntu+windows only) or the gated tauri-bundle job.

Pre-push self-checks: run `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/routing/Cargo.toml --check` and `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/orchestrator-core/Cargo.toml --check` from hybrid-orchestrator (rustfmt needs no network) and fix any formatting. Self-audit ALL new routing code and doc comments against the clippy -D warnings lint list in context.json environment_constraints (unused imports, dead_code, useless_vec, collapsible_if/match, needless Debug-format of trait objects, doc_overindented_list_items). Confirm no {workspace=true} appears in routing/Cargo.toml.
acceptance_criteria: routing/src/policy.rs defines RoutingPolicy (async trait), RoutingRequest, RoutingDecision, ManualRoute (reused from domain), RouteSource (reused), PrivacyTag (reused), AvailableModel (reused from providers), and CostBudget per Section 6.1.

routing/src/signals.rs implements complexity estimation, privacy hard-constraint evaluation, and cost signals with optional budget; each has unit tests; the pricing source (providers::AvailableModel.price; local=zero) is documented.

AutoDefaultPolicy filters by hard constraints FIRST (privacy + required capabilities), fails closed on an unsatisfiable LocalOnly/Confidential tag (returns Err, never cloud fallback), ranks by a quality-for-complexity + cost blend, and populates a human-readable rationale.

ManualOverrideResolver enforces per-message override > conversation pin > automatic precedence, and rejects a manual route that violates a privacy tag with an explanatory error while still delegating to the wrapped active automatic policy otherwise.
PolicyRegistry holds a selectable/persisted `active` automatic policy and its resolve() wraps the active policy in the manual-override precedence.
routing no longer exposes placeholder(); orchestrator-core smoke test references a real routing item and still compiles.

hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml moves routing to [workspace] exclude with updated comments + EXIT PATH; ci.yml adds routing fmt/build/clippy(-D warnings)/test steps to the routine build job in dependency order; matrix and tauri-bundle unchanged.
routing/Cargo.toml pins concrete version literals (no {workspace=true}) and path-deps providers + domain.

REVIEW FIXES (2026-09-06-215816-review.md, NEEDS_CHANGES -> addressed): (#4 zero-price locality misclassification - data-leak, FIXED fail-closed) Locality for the PRIVACY hard constraint no longer trusts price==ZERO. Added RoutingRequest.local_provider_ids: BTreeSet<String> (the caller-supplied set of PROVABLY-local provider instance ids) and signals::is_provably_local(candidate, set). AutoDefaultPolicy::filter_candidates and ManualOverrideResolver::resolve_manual now gate LocalOnly/Confidential on membership in that set, not on a zero price - so a mispriced/zero-priced CLOUD model can never satisfy a privacy tag (fails closed to PrivacyConstraintUnsatisfiable / ManualRouteRejected). is_local_price is retained but restricted to the COST signal only (estimate_cost) and the PreferLocal ranking nudge now also uses provable locality. Updated module docs (auto_default, signals) to explain price is a cost signal, not proof of locality. New unit tests: zero_priced_cloud_is_not_local_under_privacy_tag, priced_local_is_allowed_under_privacy_tag_when_provably_local (auto_default), manual_route_to_zero_priced_cloud_is_rejected_under_privacy_tag (manual_override), provable_locality_keys_off_the_set_not_price (signals). (#1 persona default_route ignored - FIXED) AutoDefaultPolicy::decide now honors persona.default_route as a soft preference BELOW the pin/override (handled by the wrapping resolver) and ABOVE automatic ranking: if the default route survived the hard-constraint filter it is selected with a 'persona default route ...' rationale; it never overrides a privacy/capability constraint. Tests: persona_default_route_is_honored_when_it_survives_filter, persona_default_route_ignored_when_filtered_out. (#3 manual pin vs enumeration failure - JUSTIFIED, kept fail-closed) A manual route absent from the freshly-enumerated `available` list is still rejected as ManualRouteUnavailable rather than trusted blind: Section 6.3 requires manual routes to STILL pass hard-constraint validation, and honoring an unenumerated pin would bypass the privacy/capability gate (a leak risk under a privacy tag - we could not prove the pinned model is local). Made the failure mode EXPLICIT: the error message now names the transient-enumeration possibility and advises retry. All existing routing test helpers updated to populate local_provider_ids. rustfmt --check clean for routing.
